jira.settingsDesc: Base URL, email and API token of your own Jira instance. The token is stored encrypted in the OS keychain and is never handed back to the UI.
jira.enabledHint: While it is off the agent sees no Jira tools at all, so no tokens are spent on tool descriptions.
jira.tokenHint: Stored in the OS keychain, not in localStorage. The field is cleared after saving and the token is never shown again.
jira.allowCommentsHint: Also exposes the tool that reads the latest comments on a ticket.
jira.allowSearchHint: Without this the agent may only read the tickets linked here. With it, it may search and read any ticket your account can see.
jira.readOnlyNote: Every Jira tool is read-only: only HTTP GET requests are sent. Creating, editing, commenting and transitioning are not implemented.
jira.invalidKey: Invalid issue key. Expected the form ABC-123.
jira.notConfigured: No Jira access stored — Settings → Jira.
jira.toolNote: Claude Code gets the tools in-process, OpenCode per session over ACP. Codex and Cursor need the entry in their configuration.
jira.registerExternalHint: Codex and Cursor read MCP servers only from their own configuration. l8git adds the server there (~/.codex/config.toml and ~/.cursor/mcp.json) and removes it again once the switch is off. That also makes the entry visible in your own Codex and Cursor sessions. Claude Code and OpenCode do not need it.
jira.linkDialogDesc: The ticket applies to this conversation only. The agent may read linked tickets and nothing else.
jira.panelHint: Tickets are linked per conversation: right-click a chat in the sidebar → “Link Jira ticket”. Key and status then show in the chat row.
jira.sessionNote: A linked ticket takes effect immediately, even in a chat that is already running. The switches above only apply to chats started afterwards — the CLI asks for the tool list once, when it connects.
